cohort: The study included 165 pregnant women with singleton term pregnancies admitted to a labour ward for delivery, presenting with suspicious/pathological CTG traces or meconium-stained liquor with normal CTG traces.
finding: Abnormal CTG is a poor predictor of fetal acidosis and neonatal status after birth but a good predictor of the presence and grade of meconium-stained liquor.
cross-section timing: Cord blood collected immediately after birth; CTG traces monitored during labour.
